Chapter 5: Tools & Environment Used

5.1 Hardware and Software Requirements

The AssetDesk engineering platform leverages modern web standards, an asynchronous runtime, and a document database. Environment specifications are partitioned into verified software dependency versions and physical workstation hardware profiles.

5.2 Server-Side and Client-Side Tooling Architecture

AssetDesk strictly decouples the client application from the backend API server. Communication occurs exclusively over stateless HTTP/JSON interfaces. Tables 5.4 and 5.5 detail the exact package ecosystem utilized, while Figures 5.1 and 5.2 depict the 3-tier logical architecture and production deployment layout.

Table 5.4: Client-Side Tooling Ecosystem
Package Version Client Function
react 18.3.1 Component UI tree
react-router-dom 6.28.1 Client-side SPA routes
axios 1.7.9 HTTP client with interceptors
vite 5.4.11 ESM dev server & bundler
eslint 8.57.1 Static code quality linting
base.css Custom Design token system
Table 5.5: Server-Side Framework & Middleware Stack
Package Version Security & Functional Role
express 4.21.2 RESTful routing & dispatch
mongoose 8.9.5 ODM schemas & validation
jsonwebtoken 9.0.2 Signed token issuance & verify
bcryptjs 2.4.3 10-round salted password hash
helmet 8.0.0 11 secure HTTP response headers
cors 2.8.5 Whitelisted origin restrictions
express-rate-limit 7.5.0 Sliding window DDoS defense
express-validator 7.2.1 Body/param schema sanitization
node-cron 3.0.3 Daily automated license scan
nodemailer 6.9.16 SMTP notification transport
Depicts clear tier boundaries: Presentation (React SPA), Application (Node.js/Express REST API controllers), and Data Layer (MongoDB with replica set resilience).
Illustrates production topology: HTTPS edge termination via NGINX reverse proxy, Node.js PM2 process clustering, and TLS connection pooling to MongoDB Atlas.
